functions.name: Reset_Entry
functions.notes: Reset vector `80:8858` jumps here. The routine executes `CLC; XCE`, establishes 8-bit A / 16-bit index mode, disables interrupts, then tail-jumps to `80:91DC` for stack/direct-page, PPU/CPU register and WRAM initialization before entering the normal startup chain.

functions.name: CartridgeMemorySelfTest
functions.notes: Called during startup at `80:886D`. It probes mirrored/available memory through `77:0000/1FFF`; success restores the original byte and `RTL`s, while failure deliberately tail-jumps to `80:94EB`.

functions.name: Fatal_GamePakNotFound
functions.notes: Failure target of `CartridgeMemorySelfTest`. Its stream at `80:9505` uses resolved frontend controls `F9/FC/FF` around the literal `game_pak_not_found`, proving normal return from the `80:C3AB` call on this path.

functions.name: Main_StateDispatchLoop
functions.notes: Repeated top-level loop. After housekeeping it indexes state `$9B`, loads one of six handler addresses from the word table at `80:88B2`, pushes synthetic return `80:88AD` with `PER`, and `JMP ($005D)`s to the selected mode handler. Returning handlers land at `80:88AE` and branch back to `80:8881`.

functions.name: Frontend_TextCommandStream
functions.notes: Nitrodon bank-80 disassembly shows a byte-command parser with control bytes `>= 0xEE`, text/layout handlers, and returns through `80:C440`; bounded historical replay tracing executes this interpreter during frontend transition construction.

functions.name: Frontend_TextCommandDispatch
functions.notes: Exact instruction `JMP ($005D)`. Canonical-ROM decoding maps valid commands `FF..EF` to 17 concrete bank-80 handlers at `80:C3CB`; run `36795810324` proves live execution. `EE` is a boundary escape/sentinel whose computed next word is not a valid ROM handler, leaving only a range-proof invariant rather than unknown targets. See `analysis/generated/frontend-text-command-dispatch.md`.

functions.name: Interrupt_LongVector73
functions.notes: Exact `JMP [$0073]`. The only explicit complete 24-bit construction found in banks 80-83 is `82:D73B-D742`, which sets `$73:$75 = 80:85A4` while interrupts are disabled during interrupt/HDMA setup.

functions.name: Interrupt_LongVector53
functions.notes: Exact `JMP [$0053]`. Complete paired assignments set `$53:$55` to `80:F60C`, `80:8610`, or `80:85A5`; the same vector is invoked by wrapper `80:B0DE`. See `analysis/generated/remaining-indirect-vector-map.md`.

functions.name: Course_SampleRuntimeSurface
functions.notes: Common per-racer 383-byte routine called from both player paths after collision/contact-shape construction and before later collision handling. It transforms course-relative state and samples both materialized runtime planes at `7E:C000` and `7E:A000/A001`. Full four-ROM structure is proven: PAL prototype and Europe at shift -32; legacy beta byte-identical. Exact meanings of individual surface values remain intentionally open.

functions.name: HUD_QueueMessage
functions.notes: Long-entry wrapper for `81:C5B3`, the confirmed per-player 32-entry message-ring enqueue routine. P1 uses storage `0CBB+` with indices `0CE1/0CE3`; P2 uses `0CE5+` with `0D0B/0D0D`. Stunt finalization calls this with wipeout/head-bounce/tabletop/trick/praise IDs. Cross-build correspondence: PAL prototype `81:C590`; Europe retail `81:C59C`, independently corroborated by two coherent direct callers.

functions.name: Stunt_FinalizeAndScoreAirTricks
functions.notes: Nitrodon's focused `stunts.txt` plus bank-82 listing expose the complete landing/finalization pipeline: roll/flip quarter-turn accumulation, half-twist conversion, Z-flip/tabletop handling, wipeout/headbounce checks, trick-message selection, stunt-combination indexing, praise lookup, and reset of transient stunt state.

functions.name: Player_ApplyVerticalAcceleration
functions.notes: Nitrodon's bank-82 annotation is directly supported by the instruction flow: current-player Y velocity is capped below `0x0200`, upward motion receives +19, downward acceleration is `19 - Yvel/32`, the result is added to Y velocity, and current-player Y coordinate is incremented. Structural equivalents: PAL prototype `82:A959` (strong, 91.2% byte similarity); Europe retail `82:A96F` (supported, 89.7%), with projected operands following established regional WRAM-motion families.

functions.name: Input_DecodePlayer1Buttons
functions.notes: Nitrodon's bank-82 listing shows raw controller words `$030D/$030F` decoded into explicit A/X/L/R/B/Y/select/start flags and normalized vertical/horizontal direction fields at `$0311/$0315`. Structural equivalents: PAL prototype `82:AA5F` (strong, 98.8% byte similarity) and Europe retail `82:AA75` (strong, 84.6%); Europe coherently shifts the controller-state block by +4 (`030D→0311` through `0335→0339`).

functions.name: RNC1_Unpack
functions.notes: Identified by unique opcode-structure match to preserved 1992 SNES `RNC_1.S`; ROM offset `0x00B8F1`. Regional/build equivalents: Europe retail `01:B8E2` (`0x00B8E2`), 1994-11-29 PAL prototype `01:B8D1` (`0x00B8D1`), legacy beta identical to USA.

functions.name: RNC1_MakeHuffTail
functions.notes: Preserved Method-1 MAKEHUFF tail begins here; final RTS at `01:BB6E`, establishing the shipped generic RNC1 body end.

functions.name: RNC1_ReadWordLoROMSafe
functions.notes: Integration helper used by the shipped Method-1 decoder for a 16-bit packed-stream read through `IN`. Normal path returns `LDA [IN]` while restoring the pointer; when `IN=$FFFF`, it fetches the high byte from next-bank `$8000`, matching LoROM linear-stream continuity across a bank boundary. `01:BB73` is the helper's wrap-test `BNE`, not a store.

functions.name: APU_UploadBlockById_Wrapper
functions.notes: Exact bytes `JSR $8082; RTL`. Callers load X with audio block IDs before entering; the body at `02:8082` performs the SPC handshake and calls `APU_ResolveBlockPointer` at `02:812A`, establishing X as a block-record selector.

functions.name: APU_ResolveBlockPointer
functions.notes: Exact static routine maps block ID X onto the packed audio-record pool beginning at `10:8000`. It walks X length-prefixed records, performing LoROM bank-wrap arithmetic, and returns the selected record pointer in DP `$63-$65`. Package-table IDs `$00-$31` address the first 50 records, but direct setup calls pass IDs through at least `$42`; the same contiguous parser resolves records `$32-$42`. Therefore `$00-$31` is the package-table ID universe, not the resolver's upper bound.

functions.name: Text_HandleFCPositionControl
functions.notes: Bounded static analysis of the Sayans translation-control grammar. The routine preserves A, recognizes low-byte `FC`, consumes the following parameter, scans subsequent character bytes until `FF` or `FB`, consults `Text_TestCharacterMetadataBit7` for ordinary bytes, then computes `parameter * 32 + horizontal adjustment` into DP `$9F`. The 32-column arithmetic and translated `FF FC xx` / `FB FC xx` sequences support a centered tilemap-position/layout role. Exact user-facing meaning of the parameter remains unpromoted.

functions.name: Text_TestCharacterMetadataBit7
functions.notes: Shared helper reached from four text/layout loops including `03:8998`, `00:C4CB`, and `00:C510`. It indexes the byte table at `00:C6F8` by character code and tests bit 7. Printable-table inspection shows uppercase A-Z in the low half while lowercase a-z, digits and much punctuation usually carry bit 7; therefore this is a verified character-metadata class test, not yet a proven glyph-width flag. Structural equivalents: Europe retail `80:8C41` (supported, 84.6% byte similarity) and PAL prototype `80:8C3C` (strong, 92.3%).

functions.name: Course_LoadAndMaterialize
functions.notes: Course-load orchestration called from race setup at `82:DE0F`. It selects the course resource from `77:074A`, invokes the generic resource loader with destination bank `$7F` so the RNC path decodes into `7F:0000`, then parses that payload into VRAM and runtime structures including `7E:A000` and `7E:C000`. This matches the independently verified active decoded-course payload.

functions.name: Race_UpdateRacersFrame
functions.notes: Frame-level racer orchestration. It marshals player 1 persistent state/input into the shared `$0Fxx` current-player workspace, runs collision/stunt/physics helpers including `Stunt_FinalizeAndScoreAirTricks` and `Player_ApplyVerticalAcceleration`, writes results back to player-1 slots, then conditionally repeats the same pipeline for player 2 before returning at `82:9384`.

functions.name: Race_BuildRacerOAMState
functions.notes: Per-frame racer sprite/OAM composition, long-entry wrapper at `82:ACA1`, called from the race loop at `83:CD77` after racer simulation/state fetch. It projects both racers relative to camera/viewport bounds, writes screen-coordinate and sprite-attribute state under `$1501-$1510`, and constructs high-OAM control bytes at `7E:20A2/20A3`; later `82:D2xx-D34F` code commits assembled OAM data to `$2104`.

functions.name: Race_FilterVramUpdateListsByCameraWindow
functions.notes: Filters the two compact race VRAM update lists against camera/window edge classes. List A uses count `$0DCD`, destinations `$0D8D+2*i`, selectors `$0D6D+i`, and camera inputs `$0505/$050D/$04F5`; list B mirrors this at `$0DCF/$0DAD/$0D7D` with `$0507/$050F/$04F7`. Matching an edge clears the selector/eligibility byte; destination words remain intact.

functions.name: PPU_EmitFilteredVramUpdateLists
functions.notes: Direct hardware consumer for the two filtered update lists. Iterates each count in reverse, writes destination words from `$0D8D/$0DAD` to `$2116`, indexes the 16-bit data table at `7E:2132` from selector bytes `$0D6D/$0D7D`, applies `XBA`, and stores the result through `$2118`. This is the presentation-emission seam, not gameplay activation.

functions.name: Race_UpdateCameraAndPrepareVramStrips
functions.notes: Race-frame camera update body called through long wrapper `81:A52B` from `83:CD55`. It advances camera position from `$04F5/$04F9`, derives entering-edge/ring coordinates and strip counts, then calls `81:AB88` at `81:A59A` to materialize pending VRAM-strip DMA descriptors.

functions.name: Race_BuildCameraVramDmaDescriptors
functions.notes: Converts camera-derived edge coordinates (`$0505/$0509/$050D/$0511`) and split counts (`$052B/$052F/$0533/$0537`) into up to eight DMA descriptor slots. Each slot records a ready flag, low-WRAM source, byte count, VRAM destination and VMAIN mode in `$03B9/$0399/$03A9/$03C9/$03D9 + 2*n`. Run `36966728136` observes horizontal slot 2 preparing one 32-byte entering column during steady rightward scroll.

functions.name: PPU_ConsumeCameraVramDmaDescriptors
functions.notes: NMI-side consumer reached from `80:87E1 -> 82:D197`. It scans the camera-strip descriptor ready flags in reverse slot order, clears each active flag, programs `$2116`, DMA source `$4302`, size `$4305` and `$2115`, then triggers channel 0 through `$420B` to B-bus `$2118`. In the retained Dragster scroll, steady horizontal descriptors are consumed in the same guest frame in which `81:AB88` builds them.

functions.name: PPU_LoadPaletteAssetToCGRAM
functions.notes: Writes the caller-supplied CGRAM start index X to `$2121`, resolves asset A through the five-byte table rooted at `82:B32F`, and streams the resolved payload to `$2122`. Race setup uses this path for racer palette assets `0x06 + selector`; the representative 2P fixture resolves exact assets `0x06/0x07`.

functions.name: PPU_LoadAssetToVRAM
functions.notes: Resolves asset A through the five-byte table at `82:B32F` and streams or dispatches the resource into caller-selected VRAM destination X. Race presentation setup at `82:E02E` uses this path for exact OBJ graphics assets `0x7F` → VRAM `$0000` and `0x80` → `$1000`; both are raw in the USA ROM and round-trip byte-for-byte as 75 and 30 native 4bpp tiles.

functions.name: Race_LoadPresentationAssets
functions.notes: Race presentation setup for the proven racer family. Loads OBJ graphics resources `0x7F/0x80` to VRAM `$0000/$1000`, other race graphics resources to `$2000/$7000`, shared palettes, and player-colour palette assets `0x06 + selector` into OBJ CGRAM slots. Exact racer graphics/palette provenance is retained in `analysis/generated/racer-presentation-family.json`.

functions.name: RacerPresentation_ResolveFramePointer
functions.notes: Maps a 16-bit racer presentation ID to the three-byte table at `20:8000 + id*3`; the first two bytes are the source address and the third is added to bank base `0x23`. Exact ROM-backed round trips for fixture IDs `0540/0542/0544/057E` are recorded in `analysis/generated/racer-presentation-family.json`.

functions.name: RacerPresentation_DecodePackedFramePair
functions.notes: Consumes frame pointers resolved by `83:F296`, interprets mask/header fields and packed 16-bit words, and feeds the race-render tile/presentation construction path. Remaining packed-word meanings are intentionally left for on-demand renderer work.

functions.name: Race_HandleCheckpointFinish
functions.notes: Runtime course-object code `0x14` dispatches here through `81:8320`. The handler gates on per-player `$119D/$119F`, snapshots race time, decrements `$0EF1/$0EF3` laps, and advances `$1199/$119B`. Run `36801728342` dynamically reproduces identical progression through stock Dragster results. Cross-build correspondence: PAL prototype `81:8050`; Europe retail `81:8050`, independently confirmed by the relocated object-code `0x14` dispatch table. Comparative analyzer evidence shows Europe retail alone contracts the frame-normalization sub-block at `81:8102` from the 22-byte USA/beta/PAL-prototype shape to 8 bytes, after which the handler continues at a -14-byte shift.

cross_build.independent_evidence: relocated object-dispatch table maps object code 0x14 directly to 81:8050
